text: {"score":3,"justification":"Core numbers match the card: 17.5% of 955 claims, expected 3.1%, score 8.86, z 2.36, 45 documented, 20 documented 99215 with 2 below billed (10% vs 0%), and 4 of 36. The language is cautious and the next steps are concrete. However, several claims are unsupported or misframed, and the investigator would need to redo some of the analysis. The figure 24 (problems 24%) and the other note-check shares (late 7%, data 9%, unsigned 0%) are not on the card and could only come from tool output that is not shown, so they are ungrounded here. The summary also says 'about three to four times the all-provider share in every tier', but the ratios by tier range from about 3.7x (0 conditions) to 4.5x (2 conditions), and about 2.5x for 5+ conditions, so 'roughly three to four times' is loose. The statement that 18 of 20 documented 99215 claims were 'supported' is derived, not directly stated. Citing C0015212 as 'also flagged for data reviewed' is not verifiable from the card. The headline says the sample 'mostly supports the billed level', yet the rationale argues the documentation may be inflated, which is somewhat contradictory. C0015159 is cited as an example of 0-condition back pain, rash or URI, but it is J06.9 (URI) only; the back pain claim is C0015252, and rash is not shown anywhere. The hedging is reasonable, but the mixed signal and unverifiable claims reduce usefulness.","problems":["Note-check percentages (problems 24%, late 7%, data 9%, unsigned 0%) are not on the evidence card; 24 was flagged by the number check","'Rash' complaint is not supported by any cited claim's dx; the cited claims show R10.9, J06.9 and M54.50","'Roughly three to four times in every tier' is imprecise; the 5+ tier ratio is about 2.5x and the 2-condition tier about 4x","Claim that C0015212 was 'also flagged for data reviewed' is not verifiable from the card","Headline says charts 'mostly support' billed level while the body suggests documentation may be inflated, which muddles the message","Next step names only three claims and gives no explicit sample size; the two 'examples' fixed-format lines repeat content already in the text"]}
